tanggal: 8th of Shawwal, one week after Eid al-Fitr (annual)
lokasi: Krapyak, Linggoasri, and various districts in Pekalongan City
deskripsi: Syawalan is the second 'Eid' for the people of Pekalongan, with festivities that for some residents even surpass Eid al-Fitr itself[cite: 2]. Falling on the 8th of Shawwal, this celebration is rooted in the tradition of ending the six-day sunnah fast in the month of Shawwal and has evolved into a city-wide cultural festival that has taken place for hundreds of years[cite: 2]. The series of events is diverse, ranging from the cutting of a MURI-record-breaking giant lopis in Krapyak, the 'gunungan megono' parade in Linggoasri, to the creation of hundreds of meters of 'getuk lindri'[cite: 2]. This tradition serves as a cultural tourism attraction that illustrates the culinary richness and togetherness of the people of Pekalongan[cite: 2].

lokasi: Hoegeng Stadium and fields in the four districts of Pekalongan City
deskripsi: The Balloon Festival Week was initiated by the Pekalongan City Government and the 'Sedulur Balon' community to accommodate the tradition of flying hot air balloons during Syawalan safely and orderly, while also curbing the practice of illegal balloon flights that endanger air traffic[cite: 2]. Preliminary rounds are held at the district level, with the best teams advancing to the grand final, which is usually centered at Hoegeng Stadium[cite: 2]. Competition judging criteria include balloon motifs, team coordination, diameter, and perfection during flight[cite: 2]. The festival involves many parties, including AirNav Indonesia, PLN, and BMKG to ensure flight safety, and it consistently attracts thousands of residents every year[cite: 2].

lokasi: Jetayu Cultural Tourism Area & Pekalongan Batik Museum
deskripsi: Nusantara Batik Week is a grand annual event that reaffirms Pekalongan's position as the World Batik City, with approximately 70% of national batik production originating from this city[cite: 2]. Centered in the Jetayu Cultural Tourism Area and the Batik Museum, the festival presents batik exhibitions from Pekalongan and various other regions in Indonesia, MSME bazaars, public services such as vehicle registration (Samsat) and immigration, as well as local culinary delights[cite: 2]. This event serves as a showcase for the batik-based creative economy and a gathering space for families, and it continues to grow as a national-scale tourism magnet[cite: 2].

tanggal: January–March, following the Lunar New Year celebration (annual)
lokasi: Po An Thian Temple area, Jalan Blimbing, East Pekalongan
deskripsi: The Pintoe Dalem Street Fair is a Chinese New Year night bazaar whose roots are said to date back to the 1930s and serves as a symbol of inter-religious harmony in Pekalongan[cite: 2]. Held for three days around the Po An Thian Temple, this festival features dozens of halal and non-halal culinary tenants, lion dance (barongsai) attractions, Chinese cultural parades, and music stages[cite: 2]. The peak of the Lunar New Year series is usually closed with a Sacred Parade and a serving of 'Lontong Cap Gomeh'[cite: 2]. This event is open to the public and is always visited by citizens of various ethnicities and religions[cite: 2].

lokasi: Jalan Truntum, Krapyak Village, North Pekalongan
deskripsi: The Krapyak Suro Porridge Festival is held by the residents of Krapyak Village every year to welcome the Islamic New Year (1 Muharram) with the tradition of distributing 'suro' porridge[cite: 2]. This three-day event combines elements of tradition, MSME empowerment, and cultural tourism, complete with creative economy stalls and management support from the local Tourism Office[cite: 2]. The festival continues to be developed to be more structured and have a broad impact on the local economy, while maintaining the religious traditions of the coastal people of Pekalongan[cite: 2].

The 'Ayo Membaca' (Let's Read) Literacy Festival is an annual agenda of the Pekalongan City Archives and Library Office to increase public interest in reading[cite: 2]. For several days, the Jetayu Sports Hall (GOR) is transformed into a center for literacy activities that combine book exhibitions, various literacy competitions, MSME bazaars, writing workshops, and art performances[cite: 2]. This festival is designed not just as a ceremony, but as a continuous effort to improve the reading culture and literacy index of the people of Pekalongan City[cite: 2].

Every October 2nd, Pekalongan City holds a series of activities to commemorate National Batik Day, including cultural discussions that bring together the government, academics, batik village associations, vocational students, communities, and batik industry players[cite: 2]. This moment reaffirms Pekalongan's status as a UNESCO Creative City in the Craft and Folk Art category, while serving as a venue to strengthen the batik ecosystem to face global challenges[cite: 2]. The event is usually centered in the Batik Museum courtyard with a reflective atmosphere that also celebrates the city's cultural identity[cite: 2].

lokasi: Coastal beaches and Pekalongan fishing port
deskripsi: Sedekah Laut or Sadranan is an annual thanksgiving tradition for Pekalongan fishermen for the marine catch they have obtained throughout the year[cite: 2]. On the day of the event, fishermen do not go to sea and distribute the sea's bounty to local residents through art performances, competitions, and cheap markets[cite: 2]. The core procession consists of floating offerings in the form of boat replicas into the middle of the sea, also enlivened by 'sintren' arts, 'ruwatan' shadow puppet shows, and local community cultural parades[cite: 2]. This tradition is a strong reflection of the life of the coastal community of Pekalongan, which is integrated with the sea[cite: 2].
